quiz_title: 📱 App Challenge 4: Math Quiz Screens & Variables

questions.question: How do you create a multi-screen application in MIT App Inventor?
options: You can't, apps only have 1 screen
By clicking the 'Add Screen...' button in the Designer header
By drawing a square on canvas
questions.explanation: Correct! The 'Add Screen...' button allows developers to create Screen2, Screen3, and more.

questions.question: Which control block is used to open a completely different screen inside your app?
options: open another screen with start value
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'open another screen' block takes a text string representing the exact name of the screen to open.

questions.question: What happens to the current screen when the 'close screen' block is executed?
options: The current active screen is closed, returning the player to the previous screen
questions.explanation: Perfect! The 'close screen' block terminates the current layout view, revealing the screen that opened it.

questions.question: If you want to send a player's score to a second screen (like a result screen), which block should you use?
options: open another screen with start value (screenName, startValue)
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 'open another screen with start value' block opens the target page and passes variables or values along.

questions.question: How does the second screen retrieve the score or start value sent by the first screen?
options: Using the 'get start value' control block
questions.explanation: Great! The 'get start value' block returns the exact data value passed during screen transition.

questions.question: In a Math Quiz app, how do we initialize a global variable named 'Score' to 0?
questions.explanation: Excellent! We use the orange 'initialize global variable to' block and snap a math 0 block to it.

questions.question: Which block increases our global variable 'Score' by 1 point when a player gets an answer right?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Getting the current value of the variable, adding 1, and saving it back is the correct syntax to increment counters.

questions.question: What block is used to make a choice or decision in blocks programming (e.g. check if player's answer is correct)?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 'if-then' control block checks a boolean condition and executes code inside if it is true.

questions.question: How can you check if the answer typed in TextBoxAnswer.Text is exactly equal to '10'?
questions.explanation: Great! Tapping the comparison (=) math block inside the if condition checks matching answers.

questions.question: Which component is excellent for displaying the final score on the result screen?
questions.explanation: Perfect! A Label is perfect for displaying text values like 'Your Score is 5' by setting its Text property.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to navigate to a screen named 'ScreenResult' and pass the value of a global variable named 'Score' when a button is clicked.
questions.task_hint: when ButtonFinish.Click -> open another screen with start value(screenName='ScreenResult', startValue=get global Score)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! This is the standard procedure to pass game statistics across screens in App Inventor.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code for an if statement: if TextBox1.Text is equal to '5', then set LabelFeedback.Text to 'Correct!', else set LabelFeedback.Text to 'Wrong!'
questions.task_hint: if TextBox1.Text == '5' then set LabelFeedback.Text to 'Correct!' else set LabelFeedback.Text to 'Wrong!'
questions.explanation: Perfect! Using if-else choices provides immediate feedback to students!
